elements.element: Customer has the right to terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1A expressly provides that “Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience.”

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days’ prior written notice to Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1A requires “30 days’ prior written notice to Commerce One.”

elements.element: Upon Customer’s termination for convenience, Vendor must refund prepaid fees pro rata for the period after termination becomes effective.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1A requires Commerce One to refund “any prepaid fees on a pro-rata basis for the period after the effective date of termination.”

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1A expressly states that Commerce One has no termination-for-convenience right “during any committed term.”

elements.element: Customer has the right to terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1A expressly grants Customer a termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: Customer termination for convenience requires 60–90 days’ prior notice.
elements.evidence: The operative notice period is 30 days, not a notice period within the specified 60–90-day fallback range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer must not exceed three months’ fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed by the supplied operative language, so the condition triggering the cap is absent.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1A prohibits Commerce One from terminating for convenience during a committed term, while Section 11.1 permits either party to terminate or prevent renewal at term expiration.

elements.element: Vendor must provide 90 days’ prior notice to terminate for convenience at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 permits either party to provide only 30 days’ notice before term expiration; no 90-day Vendor notice requirement appears.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the preferred position: Customer receives a 30-day convenience-termination right, a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and protection against Vendor convenience termination during a committed term. It does not fully implement the fallback because the specified 60–90-day Customer notice period and 90-day Vendor notice period are absent. The change is substantively minimal and does not disturb the existing cause-based termination rights or term structure, although placing Section 11.1A after Section 11.2 is slightly awkward.
